paragraphs.text: The Radix was a site in the very center of the Tangle on the plane Mirrodin , which became the site of the green lacuna . The Araneas Altar was built around it.

The Radix appeared as a humming sphere of brilliant green metal in a perfectly circular clearing of burnished copper one hundred feet across at the heart of the Tangle . It was devoid of trees and gelfruit. No vorracs or any other animals were ever seen inside it. No mold accumulated here, and the Radix was warm to the touch even at the black sun’s noon. It was considered sacred to the elves and Sylvok druids of the Tangle, as anything left on its surface slowly vanished in a matter of days, with the rare exception of the Heartwood Shard . It was the place where the Viridian elves sent their honored dead to the afterlife, and also where they banished the devices and machines they deemed unnatural. They otherwise shunned the area.

Once Glissa tapped a large amount of mana to destroy the Kaldra Champion, a surge of green mana from Mirrodin's Mana Core discharged through the Radix and ascended to become Mirrodin's fifth moon, effectively destroying the Radix and forming the Green Lacuna in its place.

After the fifth dawn, strange, metallo-organic growths began to sprout around and within the lacuna. The elves also consider these growths, called lamina, and the Radix itself, sacred. The Sylvok built a shrine around the Radix. They called it the Araneas Altar , an eight-sided construct to honor Lord Araneas . Crafted from found metal, the Altar resembles a giant metal spider when viewed from above. The "heart" of the spider is the giant hole that was formerly the Radix.
